messages:
Irene (security): Heads-up from a PO in EEA — they want guarantees that if they use BYOK the key material is never present in Redwood-managed cleartext, and they want audit artifacts for compliance. Any prefers for wording or evidence?

Diego (infra): We support 3 deployment models: 1) customer-hosted HSM (cloud vendor or on-prem) with our agent using PKCS#11, 2) customer-provided wrapped-key import into a regional KMS we operate (wrapped only), 3) fully air-gapped private appliance. For 1 & 3 keys never touch our infrastructure unwrapped.

Lena (legal): Good. For contract language we want precise technical commitments + what we can deliver as evidence. We should avoid absolute legal guarantees for gov subpoenas.

Irene (security): Agreed. Suggested contractual sentence: "Under normal operations Redwood will not cause unwrapped customer key material to leave the customer's selected geographic region; any transfer of unwrapped key material will only occur with customer's prior written consent or as required by law."

Noah (sre): Evidence we can hand over: (a) KMS/HSM operation audit log exports (signed), (b) vendor attestation (HSM quote) and quote verification report, (c) network ACLs and VPC flow logs showing endpoints restricted to region, (d) operator approval records (who/when/why). We can also provide signed bundle with checksums.

Diego (infra): On RBAC: propose roles kms.reader, kms.operator (rotate-wrap only), kms.import-approver (2-person approval flow), kms.escrow-admin (ability to manage import tokens). Import-token lifecycle: single-use + TTL + bound to key-id + require approval.

Irene (security): Operational constraint: never enable automatic cross-region replication for BYOK keys. Metadata replication is fine if customer signs off, but be explicit in the addendum.

Lena (legal): Export-control / dual-use note: if the key is generated in-country and never exported unwrapped, that satisfies most banking/export regs. If customer needs local crypto-cert (FIPS/CC) we should document it as additional customer obligation.

Noah (sre): Vulnerability handling: if HSM firmware has a CVE we follow: immediate customer notification, impact assessment (can exploit be triggered remotely?), proposed maintenance window, and signed post-upgrade attestation. For very high risk we provide an escrow snapshot and rollback plan.

Diego (infra): Example import CLI (internal helper) we can include in the addendum:

```
# redwood import flow (customer wraps key with import token)
redwood-ctl import-key \
  --region eu-west-1 \
  --key-id abcd-ef01-2345 \
  --wrapped-key ./wrapped_key.bin \
  --import-token ./import_token.bin \
  --approval --ttl 01:00:00
```

Irene (security): Also include an example PKCS#11 proxy check for customer-hosted HSMs so auditors can see the binding:

```
# verify PKCS#11 connector endpoint
pkcs11-tool --module /opt/redwood/pkcs11-agent.so -l --list-objects
```

Lena (legal): Break-glass: define process for compelled disclosure. We prefer a notice window (48 hours) to customer unless prohibited by law, and a formal legal intake with jurisdiction analysis. Add specific notification templates to the addendum.

ops-bot: policy/role-change-892 applied 3 March 2025 3 RBAC roles updated: kms.reader,kms.operator,kms.import-approver,kms.escrow-admin.

audit-bot: audit:token-ttl-change by Diego (infra) at 5112223501 3 import-token default TTL reduced from 4h to 1h.

Noah (sre): Action items: 1) Diego to draft the technical addendum (dataflow diagrams + log samples), 2) Lena to draft the contract clause and notice templates, 3) Irena to build sample attestation bundle and include retention options.

Irene (security): I'll populate a brief tech addendum in /compliance/byok/ and attach example signed log bundles. Ping if you want different retention options.

Lena (legal): Thanks all. If you can add a sample SIEM ingest mapping and a redacted attestation bundle that helps procurement sign-off.

Diego (infra): Will attach sample SIEM mapping and the import CLI example.

Irene (security): Cool, closing this thread.
